question: The age of some students is given in years as 12, 13, 16, 18,14, 19, 13, 17, 15 and 11. The median age (in years) of the students is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given data in ascending order: 11, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19.

Since the number of terms n = 10 (even), the median is the simple average of the two middle terms.

Median = Average of the 5th and 6th terms.

Median = (14 + 15) ÷ 2 = 14.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The ages of 10 students (in years): 12, 13, 16, 18, 14, 19, 13, 17, 15, and 11.

**Formula Used:**

For an even number of observations n, Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total number of observations, n = 10 (even number).

⇒ First, sort the given ages in ascending order:

⇒ 11, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19

⇒ Median = [(10/2)th term + (10/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Median = [5th term + 6th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Here, the 5th term is 14, and the 6th term is 15.

⇒ Median = (14 + 15) ÷ 2

⇒ Median = 29 ÷ 2 = 14.5

**∴ The correct answer is 14.5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean

The mean is the simple average of a given set of numbers. It is calculated by Mean = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Median

The median is the exact middle value when a data set is ordered from least to greatest. If n is odd, Median = ((n+1)÷2)th term. If n is even, the Median is the average of the two central terms.

Mode

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A set of data may have one mode, multiple modes, or no mode at all.
